sources.title: Dependent Age Limits – Civilian and Postal Enrollees

units.heading: Age limit
units.text: Children of civilian and postal enrollees are covered until their 24th birthday.

units.heading: Student status
units.text: Full-time student status does not extend coverage for children of civilian or postal enrollees.
conditions: NOTE: There is no student extension for civilian or postal enrollees.

units.heading: Notice timing
units.text: The program mails a coverage-end notice 45 days before the child's 24th birthday.

units.heading: Age limit
units.text: Children of uniformed members are covered until their 20th birthday.

units.heading: Full-time students
units.text: A child who is a full-time student at an accredited school remains covered until the 24th birthday or graduation, whichever comes first.
conditions: ONLY IF the sponsor registered the student status in the member records system before the child's 20th birthday.

units.heading: Proof of enrollment
units.text: The carrier may request proof of full-time enrollment each school term.

units.heading: Who qualifies
units.text: A child of any age who cannot self-support because of a condition that began before the age limit may stay covered.
conditions: EXCEPTION: A physician statement must be sent within 60 days of the request.

units.heading: Information requests
units.text: Verify two approved security items before sharing account details with the enrollee.

units.heading: Account changes
units.text: Verify three approved security items before making any change to the account.

units.heading: Payer is not the enrollee
units.text: A payment may be accepted from another person without authorization if the payer's name is on the bank account.
conditions: NOTE: Do not discuss any other account details with the payer.

units.heading: Documents on file
units.text: Before discussing an account with someone other than the enrollee, check the account for a power of attorney (POA) or an authorization to disclose information (ADI).

units.heading: POA compared with ADI
units.text: A POA holder may make changes to the account. An ADI holder may discuss coverage and billing but may not make changes.

units.heading: No document on file
units.text: If no document is on file, the enrollee may give verbal authorization for this call only, after the enrollee verifies three security items.
conditions: NOTE: Verbal authorization ends when the call ends.

slides.title: Accepting a payment from a third party

units.heading: Security before payment
units.text: Collect two security items from a third party before accepting a payment from them.

units.heading: Bank details
units.text: Do not save the third party's bank details to the account.

units.heading: What to collect
units.text: Record the caller's name and relationship to the enrollee. Legal documents are not required to report a death.

units.heading: Next steps
units.text: Submit an inactivation request and tell the caller a survivor letter will be mailed within 10 business days.
conditions: DO NOT quote refund amounts or refund dates.

units.heading: Documents
units.text: Require a certified death certificate before submitting any inactivation.

units.heading: Process
units.text: Remove a former spouse effective the date the divorce is final. Ask the enrollee to email the divorce decree to the Records team.

units.heading: Process
units.text: The uniformed sponsor mails the divorce decree to the Sponsor Services unit. Removal takes 3 to 5 business days, and the sponsor must call back to confirm.

units.heading: Cold transfer steps
units.text: Use a cold transfer to send a caller to the Research team. Add the caller's member ID and the reason for the transfer to the transfer notes.
conditions: NOTE: Tell the caller they may wait on hold before you transfer.

units.heading: Warm transfer
units.text: Senior representatives escalate to Policy with a warm transfer and stay on the line to introduce the caller.

units.heading: Check-back
units.text: Check back with the caller before 2 minutes of hold time pass.

units.heading: Check-back
units.text: Check back with the caller after 4 minutes on hold.

units.heading: During open season
units.text: During open season, enrollees may change plans for any reason. The change takes effect January 1.

units.heading: Outside open season
units.text: Outside open season, a plan change requires a qualifying life event reported within 60 days of the event.
conditions: NOTE: The qualifying life event must be on the approved event list.

units.heading: Reinstatement
units.text: Reinstate previous coverage for enrollees affected by workforce changes.

units.heading: New enrollments
units.text: New enrollments begin on the first day of the first pay period after the request is received.
